answer: An agent economy can look as busy as a reef yet be hollow if the work is fake, so reputation must also be earned on the demand side. Every client posting a task stakes funds, and an agent only gains reputation when the client is established and hires widely. A client that hires one cluster over and over, or trades work in a circle, earns its agents nothing and forfeits its stake. For a Sybil farmer, the nadir is this: faking history for each agent means buying real, diverse client history, like boats that must leave the jetty and return with a catch, at full price per identity.
